entities.name: Atlantic Triangular Trade
entities.label: Movement
entities.summary: A triangular pattern of Atlantic commerce (c. 1500–1850s): European manufactured goods shipped to West Africa; enslaved Africans transported to the Americas (the Middle Passage); and sugar, tobacco, cotton, and rum shipped back to Europe. An estimated 12.5 million Africans were forcibly transported, making it the largest forced migration in history and the engine of early modern global capitalism.
